extraction.name: IFEval: Instruction-Following Evaluation for Large Language Models
extraction.description: IFEval is an evaluation benchmark for large language models that focuses on 'verifiable instructions' - instructions amenable to objective verification of compliance, such as 'write in more than 400 words' or 'mention the keyword of AI at least 3 times'. The benchmark contains 25 types of verifiable instructions and approximately 541 prompts, with each prompt containing one or more verifiable instructions.
extraction.creator: Jeffrey Zhou, Tianjian Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Siddhartha Brahma, Sujoy Basu, Yi Luan, Denny Zhou, Le Hou
extraction.inLanguage: English (with some prompts in other languages including Tamil, Thai, Vietnamese, Arabic, Hindi, Bengali, Kannada, Telugu, Marathi, Portuguese, German, Italian, Russian, Finnish, Korean, Urdu, Bulgarian, Swahili, Persian, Gujarati, Nepali, Punjabi)
extraction.citeAs: Zhou, J., Lu, T., Mishra, S., Brahma, S., Basu, S., Luan, Y., Zhou, D., Hou, L. (2023). Instruction-Following Evaluation for Large Language Models. arXiv preprint arXiv:2311.07911.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Prompts were generated through a four-step process: First, a set of base prompts with one to three randomly selected verifiable instructions appended to the end of each prompt were generated. Then, few-shot prompting was used to identify illogical prompts and remove them. As a third step, another few-shot prompting-based approach was applied to rephrase each prompt to increase diversity of phrasing. Finally, rephrased prompts were manually checked and edited one by one.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Base prompts generated using few-shot prompting combined with 25 manually defined verifiable instruction types.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Few-shot prompting was used to rephrase base prompts to increase diversity. Rephrased prompts were manually checked and edited.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Illogical prompts were identified and removed using few-shot prompting. Prompts were manually checked and edited after rephrasing.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Verification of whether an instruction is followed is performed automatically via deterministic programs. Two metrics are computed: 'strict' accuracy which uses direct verification, and 'loose' accuracy which applies transformations to the response (removing markdown font modifiers, removing first line, removing last line, and combinations) to reduce false negatives.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: To alleviate the false negative problem from naive string matching (e.g., when markdown tags like ** are used), a loose accuracy score is computed using eight transformations. However, this loose criterion may introduce false positives and is considered a complement to the original strict criterion.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Deterministic verification programs (implemented in code, released in the GitHub repository)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Future work plans include improving prompts and verifiable instructions to make them more related to real-world applications, expanding with more verifiable instructions, and supporting multi-modal use cases.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The capability of LLMs to accurately interpret and follow natural language instructions is crucial for the precision of tasks as well as the safety and reliability of their implementations. Discrepancies in following instructions can lead to unintended outputs with dire results in crucial scenarios like healthcare or autonomous systems.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The authors note that human evaluation methods lead to potential biases and inconsistencies, and model-based evaluation heavily relies on the correctness of the evaluator model. IFEval is designed to be unbiased by using objective verifiable instructions.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Very few instructions are 100% verifiable objectively and automatically - there always exist edge cases where it is hard to determine if an instruction is followed. For example, string matching may yield false negatives when markdown formatting is used. The loose criterion reduces false negatives but may introduce false positives. The current implementation could be improved by increasing diversity and quantity of verifiable instructions, and extending to multi-modal use cases.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation/Testing benchmark for assessing the instruction-following ability of Large Language Models. Used to compare different LLMs on various instruction types and to draw insights on what types of instructions are not usually followed.
